title: Which parastichies are conspicuous depends on leaf proportions, not on divergence

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Which parastichies are conspicuous depends on leaf proportions, not on divergence

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Which of the implicit spiral families is conspicuous does not depend on the angle of divergence but on the proportions of the leaves or scales, strictly on the ratio of the diagonals of the rhomboid circumscribing each leaf-area.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: conspicuous parastichies set by the ratio of the diagonals of the rhomboid circumscribing each leaf-area, not by the divergence angle

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIV: On Leaf-Arrangement, or Phyllotaxis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: the conspicuousness of one set or another does not depend upon angular divergence. It depends on the relative proportions in length and breadth of the leaves themselves; or, more strictly speaking, on the ratio of the diagonals of the rhomboidal figure by which each leaf-area is circumscribed.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XIV, “On Leaf-Arrangement, or Phyllotaxis”; topic “Conspicuous parastichies”. Scope: phyllotactic systems such as fir-cones

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: conspicuous parastichies set by the ratio of the diagonals of the rhomboid circumscribing each leaf-area, not by the divergence angle

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch14-09: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.63

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The two rival predictors permit a strong statistical comparison. However, the joint measurements needed are uncommon and likely support only selected systems without new annotation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For organ maps with measured divergence, leaf-area rhomboid diagonals and observer-independent prominence scores, regress which parastichy family is conspicuous on shape ratio versus divergence. Dominance by diagonal ratio after controlling divergence supports the claim; a strong independent divergence effect refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Shape and divergence may covary developmentally.

Few public datasets jointly measure divergence and individual organ proportions.

Conspicuousness needs a reproducible visual or image-processing definition.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The predictor Thompson specifies, the diagonal ratio of the leaf rhomb rather than the divergence angle, is a concrete measurement and yields an obvious comparison. Existing sunflower images let a team measure rhombs, but floret shape hardly varies, and the fir-cones where scale proportions do vary lack a public morphometric table. The test is well posed and currently limited to whatever images an investigator is willing to digitize.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On cones or other lattices, measure divergence angle and the ratio of the diagonals of each scale's circumscribed rhomb, and predict which parastichy family is visually dominant. The claim is supported if that diagonal ratio predicts the conspicuous family when divergence is held constant, and divergence does not predict it when the ratio is held constant.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Sunflower florets are similar in proportion, so they provide little independent variation in the rhomb.

Cone-scale proportions and divergence are not tabulated together in an open multi-species file.
